This roadmap proposes separating their searches and sending each to the right destination. The Challenge People researching rice do not all need the same page. The strategy starts by telling the two audiences apart and mapping their searches to suitable destinations.

chunks.title: Aeroplane Rice Case Study — Social Media & SEO
chunks.text: Whether priority brand and product pages are accessible and indexable How clearly pages explain product characteristics and intended uses Whether consumer and trade enquiries each have an appropriate next step How the main website directs shoppers to the retail storefront The Proposed Plan Separate the intent, then serve it. A product search, an informational search and a trade search want three different pages. Month one — technical foundation — URL structure, robots.txt, XML sitemaps, canonical tags, broken links, redirects and indexing status.

chunks.title: Aeroplane Rice Case Study — Social Media & SEO
chunks.text: Navigation between the main site and the shopping subdomain reviewed so each property has a clear purpose Three keyword groups — product searches on varieties and characteristics; informational searches on cooking and choosing rice; trade searches on supply and export, where these match the confirmed offering. Themes such as sella basmati uses, basmati for biryani and bulk basmati supplier are starting points requiring validation Month two — product and brand content — titles, meta descriptions, headings, alt text, internal links and structured data. Product pages carrying approved specifics: rice type, pack sizes, cooking applications.

Client Hiker Wolf Industry Travel & Adventure Services Lead Generation, CRO, Technical SEO, On-Page SEO, Keyword Research Engagements 2 Paid Media 2,000+ Leads, With the Junk Filtered Out The cost per lead was already good. The problem was what those leads turned out to be. The Challenge A good cost per lead is the easiest metric to hit and the easiest to be fooled by. Volume was arriving; the sales team could not do anything with it.

chunks.title: Hiker Wolf Case Study — Paid Media & SEO
chunks.text: Keep the cost per lead low without keeping the junk Stop the sales team working unqualified contacts Get intent established before the form is submitted What We Did Filter at the form, not at the follow-up. A lead that should not have been submitted costs more than one that was never generated.

chunks.title: Hiker Wolf Case Study — Paid Media & SEO
chunks.text: OTP verification on instant forms — a verified number at the point of submission, so fake and mistyped contacts never enter the pipeline Conditional logic questions — the form branches on the answers, so a low-intent path ends before it becomes a lead CRO-optimised landing pages — for the traffic that belonged on a page rather than in a form WhatsApp campaigns — meeting the audience on the channel they actually reply on Video creative to inform intent — so the person filling the form already knows what they are asking for The Impact Over 2,000 leads delivered with qualification built into the form itself, so the cost per lead stayed efficient while what arrived at the other end was worth calling.

chunks.title: Hiker Wolf Case Study — Paid Media & SEO
chunks.text: Paid Media results Volume that the sales team could actually work. 2,000+ Leads Delivered OTP Verified at Source Conditional Form Logic Video Intent-Led Creative SEO Fixing the Foundation Before Chasing Rankings Group tours, weekend getaways, treks, camping and international packages — all sitting on a site search engines could not read properly. We started there. The Challenge Hiker Wolf sells trips people search for by destination, activity, budget and date. The site had the trips. What it did not have was a structure that let a search engine connect a query to the page that answers it.

chunks.title: Hiker Wolf Case Study — Paid Media & SEO
chunks.text: Technical and on-page issues holding the whole site back No logical URL relationship between categories, destinations and individual packages No dedicated robots.txt, so crawling was left to default behaviour No keyword base to map pages against What We Did Diagnose, then structure, then target. Optimising individual pages before the site structure is sound just moves the problem around.

chunks.title: Hiker Wolf Case Study — Paid Media & SEO
chunks.text: Technical SEO audit — a full crawl of the site to surface crawlability, structure and on-page issues, and to set a baseline every later change is measured against URL structure planned — a new scheme that makes the relationship between a trip category, a destination and an individual package explicit in the path, rather than leaving it implied robots.txt created — a dedicated file so crawl access is governed by stated rules instead of defaults Seed and long-tail keyword research — built around how people actually search for travel: destinations, activities, weekend trips and package queries, not just the brand name On-page SEO review — page relevance, content structure and keyword alignment assessed, so the implementation phase has a priority order rather than a wish list The Next Phase Implementation.

chunks.title: Hiker Wolf Case Study — Paid Media & SEO
chunks.text: The recommendations get applied, target keywords get mapped to the pages that should own them, on-page elements get rewritten against that map, and performance is tracked on organic clicks, impressions, keyword positions, indexed pages and organic enquiries — the numbers that can be checked, rather than the ones that sound good. chunks.title: LIBRE Case Study — Website & Social Media

chunks.title: LIBRE Case Study — Website & Social Media
